axis_conventions.zhou_first_any_symptom: integer days relative to the first nonzero self-reported symptom-score cell digitized from Zhou Figure 2; sampling-time alignment uncertainty approximately ±1 day
axis_conventions.hakki_canonical_symptom_onset: integer days relative to self-reported canonical symptom onset; day is day+1-contact_onset because the authors' R analysis uses 1-based which() indices while the public CSV day column is zero-based
axis_conventions.jones_symptom_onset: days relative to recalled symptom onset; hospitalized-case onset alignment, peak reported 1-3 days before onset
axis_conventions.kissler_first_detectability: days relative to first PCR detectability, not symptom onset; not a candidate emission source term without an owner axis decision

direct_emitted_material.class_role: candidate source-term evidence; closest retrieved class to emission, but RNA emission is not viable-virus-weighted emission

families.description: Daily exhaled-mask RNA emission measurements from 17 onset-aligned symptomatic challenge participants, with detection probability and conditional positive magnitude kept separate from normalized mean-shape variants.
families.evidence_grade: B for emitted RNA in analogous human-challenge setting; C for transfer to viable-virus-weighted emission

measured: daily mask E-gene RNA sample positivity and log10 copies per sample as plotted
hypothesis: use as a viable-emission source shape

families.origin: F2·dig for curves and symptom cells; R/Me/Table S2 for validation counts and AUC shares; Consensus full text plus publisher figure and supplementary appendix
families.digitization_validation: Automated digitization recovered exactly 109 positive mask samples and 63 positive air samples, matching Results. Using the digitized symptom cells, mean per-participant pre-first-symptom log-AUC shares reproduce 9.57% mask (paper 10%, SD 26) with 4 positive participants and 8.52% air (paper 9%, SD 26) with 2 positive participants.
families.normalization: digitized log10 values are exponentiated to linear E-gene copies/sample before normalization; normalized shapes integrate to 1 over the tabulated support. zeros are plotted nondetections, not proof of zero emission.
families.day_resolution_and_interpolation: integer daily step function; no interpolation across missing days; outside [-5,13] deterministic shape mass is zero by truncation, not measurement
families.presymptomatic_behavior: independent measured negative-onset rows; not clamped to onset day. Participant 18 never reported symptoms and is excluded from onset-aligned means but retained as a heterogeneity caveat.

peak_position.interpretation: mass-weighted mean is dominated by sparse high-emission bursts and is not a typical-host peak

families.rise_decay_duration: multimodal and zero-inflated; no single smooth rise/decay is measured. detection probability and conditional positive log10 magnitude are the implementation-facing representation.
families.host_heterogeneity: severe overdispersion: two participants produced 86% of airborne viral RNA on three timepoints; nasal swab correlation does not determine individual emission; participant 7 emitted large quantities despite low/late symptoms.

variants.equal_weight_central: mean of per-participant normalized linear shapes, renormalized; avoids letting two high emitters define the entire shape
variants.mass_weighted_high_emitter_sensitive: cohort mean linear copies normalized; exposes the high-emission burst tail
variants.zero_inflated_daily_model: use detection_probability for occurrence and mean_log10_positive for positive magnitude; amplitude normalization remains an owner implementation decision

families.axis_definition: Days relative to the first nonzero self-reported symptom-score cell digitized from Zhou Figure 2; participant 18 has no onset axis and is excluded from onset-aligned means.

central_and_uncertainty_variants.central: equal_weight_central daily normalized shape plus zero_inflated_daily_model occurrence/magnitude table
central_and_uncertainty_variants.heterogeneity_references: digitized individual trajectories for participants 1, 5, 7, 9 and 18
central_and_uncertainty_variants.digitization_uncertainty: not numerically quantified bar-by-bar; validated by exact endpoint positive-count recovery and presymptomatic log-AUC reproduction

families.duration_tail: Observed onset-aligned support is tabulated through day 13. Day 14 has no aligned observations because late-onset participants leave the support; this is censoring, not measured zero. Episodic positive emission persists through day 13 in the digitized cohort.

viable_virus_culture_proxy.class_role: biological proxy candidate evidence; culture positivity or PFU concentration is not emitted material

families.description: Onset-aligned daily upper-respiratory PFU measurements from unvaccinated pre-alpha/alpha ATACCC cases with definitive symptom onset, using the authors' public trajectories.csv and symptoms.RDS.
families.evidence_grade: B as human community culture kinetics in an analogous setting; C as a transfer to viable-virus-weighted emission

measured: daily PFU/mL and symptom-onset data in the authors' public repository
inferred: treating pfu<=1 as the analysis' nondetect placeholder
excluding NaN PFU rows as censored missing observations rather than zeros
hypothesis: use as an emission source shape

families.origin: R plus authors' public data repository (transcribed machine-readable data); Table 1 for kinetic rates
families.axis_validation: the day+1-contact_onset transform reproduces the paper median onset-to-PFU-peak interval of 3 d. The published 7/35 (20%) presymptomatic PFU-positive fraction is recovered only when onset-day rows are included in presymptomatic counting (day+1-contact_onset <= 0); strict negative rows give 5/35. This boundary is part of the approximately ±1-day onset-alignment uncertainty.
families.normalization: PFU/mL linear values; normalized shapes integrate to 1 over tabulated observed support. pfu<=1 is treated as nondetect because the authors' analysis uses pfu>1 for positivity.
families.day_resolution_and_interpolation: integer daily observations; step function. NaN PFU rows are censored/missing and are excluded from n_observed_cases and means; they must not be interpolated or treated as zero.
families.presymptomatic_behavior: independent measured negative-onset rows. In the unvaccinated pre-alpha/alpha subset presymptomatic normalized mass is very small, but this is a swab-PFU shape, not emitted material.
families.rise: posterior mean infectious-virus growth 5.0 e-foldings/day = +2.17 log10/day, but measured during proliferation rather than as an onset-day emission slope; 95% CrI converts to +0.61 to +12.94 log10/day
families.decay: posterior mean infectious-virus decline 2.6 e-foldings/day = -1.13 log10/day; 95% CrI converts to -4.56 to -0.30 log10/day
families.duration: paper median infectious shedding 5 d (IQR 3-7); 65% culture-positive at onset+5 and 24% at onset+7 in the broader cohort
families.host_heterogeneity: community cohort, mixed ages/variants; vaccination and delta are composition confounders. This subset is small (n=13 onset-aligned).

variants.vaccinated_delta_sensitivity: not ancestral-matched; do not use for DP without owner decision

families.axis_definition: Days relative to self-reported canonical symptom onset, computed as zero-based public day + 1 - contact_onset to match the authors' one-based R indexing.

central_and_uncertainty_variants.central: unvaccinated_pre_alpha_alpha_central equal-weight normalized daily shape plus detection/conditional-positive table
central_and_uncertainty_variants.statistical_uncertainty: small n=13 principal subset; participant-day censoring is tabulated as n_observed_cases and must not be treated as zero
central_and_uncertainty_variants.rate_uncertainty: rise +0.61 to +12.94 log10/day and decay -4.56 to -0.30 log10/day after converting published credible intervals from e-foldings/day
central_and_uncertainty_variants.axis_uncertainty: strict negative onset rows versus inclusion of the onset-day boundary changes the computed presymptomatic PFU-positive fraction from 5/35 to the published 7/35

families.description: Human-challenge focus-forming-assay timing family on a broad onset-converted axis. This is a bracketed control-point family, not a digitized full curve.
families.evidence_grade: B as human-challenge culture kinetics; C as onset-axis transfer and emission transfer

measured: qPCR/FFA first quantification and peak timing
inferred: shift by symptom onset 2-4 d post-inoculation
piecewise tail slope borrowed from Hakki infectious-virus decline
hypothesis: a smooth triangle inside the bracket

families.origin: R; prior COVID-SHED-INTERVALS-01 F2·dig for peak timing/duration extrema
families.axis_definition: symptom onset is reported only as a 2-4 d post-inoculation range; use three axis-shift variants early=-2, central=-3, late=-4 rather than pretending a participant-aligned onset axis exists

control_points_post_inoculation.first_qpcr_quantifiable: about throat 1.7 d and nose 2.4 d post-inoculation
control_points_post_inoculation.ffa_start_basis: FFA was reported as initially closely paralleling qPCR, but exact separate first-FFA times were not recovered; the piecewise start is therefore a declared sensitivity point, not measured FFA onset.

families.interpolation: piecewise linear in log10 relative units through the control points; the -5 floor is declared assay-floor sensitivity, not a measured emission floor; normalize in linear space after interpolation
families.normalization: peak=1 before linear-area normalization; no absolute PFU-to-emitted-material conversion supplied
families.host_heterogeneity: young seronegative healthy adults, controlled intranasal challenge, six early participants received remdesivir; individual duration envelope is wide
families.presymptomatic_behavior: Negative-onset control points arise only through the early/central/late onset-shift bracket. They are inferred axis conversions, not participant-level measured onset-aligned rows.
families.peak_rise_decay_duration: Peak timing and positive-duration window are measured/bracketed; no dense published numeric rise or decay curve was recovered, so slopes inside each piecewise variant are interpolation only.

central_and_uncertainty_variants.axis_uncertainty: early onset shift 2 d versus late onset shift 4 d post-inoculation
central_and_uncertainty_variants.shape_uncertainty: piecewise interpolation is a declared simplification because full numeric FFA trajectories were not recovered

families.piecewise_slope_source: The -6.8 log10 relative tail offset applies Hakki 2022 infectious-virus decline (-1.13 log10/day) over approximately 6 days from peak to the central latest-viable-detection endpoint. It does not represent the shorter median FFA detection duration. This is an explicit cross-study culture-proxy inference, not a Killingley measured slope and not a blend with RNA or emission data.

families.description: Supporting duration/tail check only, not a candidate curve.
families.evidence_grade: B for hospitalized culture/RNA measurements; not implementation-shaped

rna_kinetic_sensitivity.class_role: assay-kinetic sensitivity evidence only; RNA persistence is not viable emission

families.description: Onset-relative RNA sensitivity family using Jones' large-cohort onset-of-shedding-to-peak timing, peak-before-onset bracket, post-peak RNA slope, and a declared assay-floor separation.
families.evidence_grade: B as human RNA kinetics; C as onset-axis/emission transfer
families.origin: R/Ab; exact slope and timing read in Results in Consensus full text
families.axis_definition: symptom onset; hospitalized cases place peak viral load 1-3 d before symptom onset
families.day_resolution_and_interpolation: piecewise linear in log10 relative units; normalize in linear space. The -5 log10 relative start is a declared assay-floor sensitivity spanning roughly 10^3 vs 10^8.1 copies/swab, not a measured emission floor.
families.presymptomatic_behavior: strong positive RNA before onset is intrinsic to the Jones axis; this is not viable-virus emission
families.duration_tail: RNA positivity remains long after culture positivity; do not use duration as infectious duration
families.host_heterogeneity: very large population but hospitalized-case onset alignment and PAMS heterogeneity; peak position is class-split with Hakki
families.tail_rule: Continue the post-peak -0.168 log10/day line until it crosses the declared -5 log10 assay-floor sensitivity; after that crossing the RNA sensitivity shape is zero. This is an assay-tail rule, not an infectious-period claim.
families.normalization: Peak=1 before the integer day samples are normalized so the tabulated linear shapes sum to 1. The piecewise interpolation is in log10 relative units; normalization is in linear space.

inferred: onset-axis variants within the published 1-3 day bracket
hypothesis: -5 log10 relative assay-floor start and tail truncation rule
any transfer from RNA kinetics to viable emission

central_and_uncertainty_variants.axis_uncertainty: early_peak_minus3_floor_minus5 and late_peak_minus1_floor_minus5 span the published peak 1-3 days before onset
central_and_uncertainty_variants.slope_uncertainty: post-peak decline 95% CI -0.171 to -0.165 log10/day; onset-of-shedding-to-peak 95% CI 4.04-4.60 days

families.description: First-detectability-axis RNA parameters; not an onset-relative candidate because symptom-onset timing was not recorded.
families.evidence_grade: B as acute ambulatory RNA kinetics; not onset-convertible here
families.origin: T1/R plus authors' public posterior parameter file
families.axis_transfer_to_onset: not defensible from the paper because symptom-onset timing was not recorded; use as sensitivity to proliferation/clearance only
families.normalization: No normalized onset-relative curve is supplied because the axis is first PCR detectability and cannot be transferred to symptom onset from the paper.

measured: posterior acute-infection proliferation, clearance and duration parameters

outcome_side_validation_targets.class_role: external validation checks only; never candidate source terms because exposure/contact/behavior and nonlinear dose-response are downstream in the engine

targets.use: shape validation target accounting for inference biases; not a physical emission measurement

blocked_or_not_recovered: Zhou individual participant data are not publicly downloadable; the article says de-identified data require a written approved request and data-access agreement. Figure digitization is therefore the recovered time resolution, not the underlying participant data.

Zhou does not report a viable-only time-resolved emitted-material AUC or curve. Culture-positive mask swabs are visually indicated in Figure 2, but overlapping symbols/annotations prevented a validated automated digitization of those fill states; exact time-resolved viable mask emission remains blocked.
No retrieved source directly measures emitted viable virus densely enough to report an onset-day rise slope or post-peak emission decay slope.
Kissler cannot be onset-aligned because symptom-onset timing was not recorded.
owner_decision_required_before_engine_im: Choose the endpoint priority and representation for the source term: Zhou direct emitted RNA with explicit zero-inflated host heterogeneity, Hakki/Killingley culture-proxy PFU kinetics, or a declared hybrid proxy-transfer rule. This decision must be made before any implementation because the evidence classes must not be blended silently.
